transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start off, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, doctor. Well, what brings me in is... I've been having this trouble with my eating. Once I start eating those comfort foods, I tell myself, "Maria, that is enough." But my hand just goes right back to the pot. It's like I just can’t make myself stop once I get started.

After one of these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you do anything afterward to try to get rid of the food or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising a lot?

No, no, I don't do any of that. I don't make myself throw up or take any pills or anything like that. And I'm certainly not out exercising a whole lot at my age. I just... well, I just eat the food and then sit there feeling too full and upset with myself. But I don't do anything to try and get rid of it.
How often would you say these episodes of feeling out of control with eating happen—for example, how many times per week, and how long has this been going on?

Well, it's been going on for a little while now. Since my friend passed away, I'd say this has been happening most weeks. Usually, it's about once or twice a week. It mostly happens on those quiet afternoons, you know, after I get home from choir practice or when I'm done with my gardening and there's just... nothing else going on.
During these episodes, do you tend to eat alone or hide how much you're eating because you feel embarrassed about the amount?

No, I wouldn't say I hide it or eat alone on purpose. It's just that I live by myself now, so I'm usually alone anyway when it happens. But I don't go out of my way to sneak around or hide the food from anyone. If someone were to come over, I suppose I might feel a little silly about how much I've got out, but I'm not locking the doors or hiding wrappers in the trash. It just happens when I'm on my own at the house.
Have you noticed any other changes recently, like unexplained weight gain, feeling unusually tired or sluggish, or feeling cold more often than before?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My weight has stayed about the same, I think. And I don't feel any more tired or cold than usual for someone my age. It's really just the eating that's been bothering me.

During these episodes, would you say you're eating an unusually large amount of food—more than most people would eat in that same amount of time—or is it more that you feel out of control even with a normal-sized portion?

Well, I'd say it's definitely a large amount of food. Some of those afternoons, you know, after choir or when I finish up in the garden, I'll fix myself a plate of rice and beans, or maybe some chicken stew. But then... I just keep going back for more. Before I know it, I've eaten enough for two or three meals all by myself. So yes, it's a lot more than just a normal portion.
During these episodes, do you notice yourself eating much faster than usual, and do you feel intense guilt, disgust, or depressed afterward because of how much you ate?

Well, I have always been a slow eater. But lately, when this happens... yes, I do eat fast. I'll just be standing right there by the kitchen counter, and I'm eating so quick I'm hardly even tasting the food before the next bite is already in my mouth. 

As for feeling intensely depressed or disgusted afterward... I wouldn't really use those words, no. I don't feel great about it, of course, but it's mostly just how fast I'm going that I notice.
